jobs.title: Principal Remediation Practice Lead
jobs.description:
Overview

At UES, we’re a team of more than 4,000 engineers, scientists, geologists, inspectors, technicians, and drillers united by a shared purpose—to make a meaningful impact in the communities we serve. As a national leader in geotechnical engineering, environmental consulting, and materials testing and inspection, we collaborate on transformative projects across transportation, energy, water, healthcare, and more. Learn more about the benefits of joining Team UES and our core values at careers.teamues.com.

Position Overview

Bowyer Environmental Consulting, a UES company is seeking to add a Principal Remediation Practice Lead
to support our offices in Long Beach, CA and Mission Viejo, CA. Responsibilities of this Principal role include a seller-doer focused on strategic scoping, obtaining client/agency/third party buy-in and execution of subsurface investigation/remediation programs and associated litigation support activities.

Technical scope is focused on remediation engineering, supporting environmental remediation projects involving remedial investigation, feasibility studies, pre design investigations, remedial design, remedial action, and post construction activities.

Responsibilities

Plan and coordinate work, provide technical leadership by leveraging past experience in remedial investigations, feasibility studies, pre-design investigations, remedial design, remedial action, operation and maintenance, regulatory negations/closure activities, post closure compliance and safety.
Serve as primary client contact for project scheduling, issue resolution, and invoicing.
Supervise a team of environmental professionals, specialists, and technicians conducting. Phase I, II investigations and remediation.
Build and maintain strong client relationships; support organizational networking and outreach.
Recruit, train, and mentor departmental personnel.
Identify opportunities for new business and additional project work.
Prepare accurate cost estimates and detailed proposals.
Secure signed client agreements before project initiation.
Assist in scoping project work and gathering initial client data.
Review and edit technical reports prepared by staff; prepare reports when directly involved in fieldwork or research.
Provide strategic guidance, Innovate and help advance industry remedial practice.
Typically spend approximately 80% of the time in the office (report writing/data analysis) and 20% in the field (sampling/research).
Submit accurate paperwork and documentation in a timely manner.
Monitor departmental expenses and interface with accounting for financial oversight.
Collaborate with other departments and regional offices to provide technical support.
Ensure strict adherence to company and regulatory safety procedures.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Geology, or related scientific field.
Professional Engineer (PE) or Registered Geologist (PG) license preferred.
Minimum of 10 years of experience in environmental engineering or consulting.
HAZWOPER 40-hour certification, AHERA certification, and applicable annual refreshers required.
Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook).
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to interpret technical documents and comply with regulatory standards.

Preferred Qualifications

A Professional Geology (PG) or Professional Engineering (PE) license in California.
Experience in soil vapor extraction and a range of groundwater treatment technologies (including air sparging, reductive dechlorination, oxidation and/or thermal remedial processes).
Experience in planning and implementing soil management and post remedial monitoring programs.
Ability to write technical reports, proposals, business correspondences and/or procedure manuals as needed.
Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts and draw valid conclusions.
Skilled in making presentation of technical information to staff, clients, regulators and the industry in general.

Travel Requirements

This position requires extensive travel, approximately up to 20% of the time, in support of business

objectives and client engagements. Travel may be both scheduled and on short notice, depending on

project needs. Destinations typically include job sites, field locations, or regional offices, where work may

be conducted in outdoor or operational environments. Adherence to all company safety protocols and

use of PPE is required during travel and on-site work.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

Occasionally exposed to outside weather conditions such as precipitation, extreme cold or heat, dusty and noisy work environments.
Office work requiring long-term sitting and computer work
The physical requirements for this position may include and are not limited to:o Ability to lift and/or carry up to 40 lbso Ability to stand and walk for long periods of time as well as drive long distanceso Frequent use of fingers, hands and arms for typing, cellphoneo Ability to bend, twist, reach, stoop, pull, kneel, lift, carry, and push repetitivelyo Ability to speak and hear effectively to communicate sometimes with noisy environmentso Ability to see, smell, hear and touch as well as reach, climb or balance, crouch, stoop, crawl, kneel and sito Ability to regularly lift and/or move/shake up to 40lbs. (soil and/or concrete tests and related apparatus); frequently lift and/or move up to 60lbs. (soil and sand samples, and nuclear density equipment); and occasionally move more than 100lbs. (such as a loaded wheelbarrow of concrete samples)

EEO Statement

UES is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is proud to recruit the most qualified candidates. Please see our full EEO Statement at the bottom of the page
here

USD $175,000.00 - USD $250,000.00 /Yr.

jobs.title: Graduate Environmental Scientist - January Start
jobs.location: York Street, New South Wales, Australia
jobs.description:
About Us

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real-world impact.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.

When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

A Day in the Life

Formerly known as Epic Environmental, the Australian arm of Onterris has kept the strong culture we are well known for. The team continues to work closely with clients, building trusted relationships and delivering high-quality outcomes without an overemphasis on KPIs.

Our teams have the opportunity to work alongside industry leaders, auditors, and professionals with vast experience within our industry, while enjoying regular social events and collaborative work that bring the team together. Onterris also supports career development through relevant internal opportunities and individual one-on-one career conversations focused on growth and progression.

We are seeking a Graduate Environmental Scientist to join our growing Contaminated Land and Water team out of our Sydney office. Have the opportunity to work alongside more than 50 land and water professionals across Australia who are actively invested in mentoring, collaboration and your long-term career development.

This role will be responsible for a full range of activities including:

Assisting and delivering field investigations across a variety of sites – including soil, groundwater, and surface water assessments
Preparing clear and high-quality reports
Supporting project managers and ensuring open and clear communications when in the field

Your Expertise And Skills

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management or related disciplines
0-1 years experience in contaminated land
Open C class drivers licence valid in NSW

Onterris is a leading global environmental solutions company partnering with organizations to solve complex challenges where environmental pressures, regulatory expectations and operational risks intersect. Guided by our mission to advance the way of life without compromising the integrity of our environment, we believe environmental responsibility and human progress are fundamentally connected. Our scientists, engineers, field teams and consultants apply systems thinking that unites science, data and practical expertise to deliver solutions that strengthen our clients’ resilience, mitigate risk and protect the air, water and soil that sustain communities, while uncovering responsible paths forward for planet and progress. For more information, visit www.onterris.com.

We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. We acknowledge that these experiences and perspectives help to enrich our teams and contribute to our ongoing success. We are committed to providing access and reasonable accommodation in our employment for all applicants. For US residents, click here to learn more.

jobs.title: Early-Career Environmental Scientist - Contaminated Land
jobs.description:
Great opportunity to join our long-established Contaminated Land consulting group in Perth
Enjoy mentoring and access to our senior specialists
Diverse projects and learning opportunities across multiple sectors and clients

Tetra Tech Coffey provides high-end environmental, geotechnical, digital, and engineering design consulting services in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea. Every day, our people come together to solve complex challenges for our clients.

With over 30,000 Tetra Tech colleagues across 550 offices globally, we deliver projects that improve lives through science, technology, and innovation.

About The Role

As an early-career professional, you’ll work alongside our team of experienced environmental professionals who are dedicated to helping you grow and succeed. You'll gain hands-on experience in assessing and remediating contaminated land, and developing essential skills in client engagement, proposal development, and project management.

You’ll work on a diverse range of exciting and challenging contaminated land projects across multiple industries including Defence, Mining, Oil & Gas and Government.

This is a great opportunity to grow a rewarding career in a global consultancy that values innovation, collaboration, and excellence in environmental solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct fieldwork for a variety of contaminated site investigation and remediation projects, including soil, groundwater, surface water, and ground gas sampling.
Observe, guide, and document site remediation activities to ensure compliance and effectiveness.
Manage, interpret, and ensure the quality of data through rigorous quality assurance and quality control processes.
Assist in writing proposals, project correspondence, and technical reports to communicate findings and recommendations effectively.

About You

To thrive in the role, you should ideally demonstrate the following:

A degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or Geosciences.
A minimum of 12 months gained in contaminated land fieldwork.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, enabling you to convey complex information clearly and effectively.
Excellent interpersonal skills with a collaborative team-oriented mindset.
Genuine enthusiasm for producing high-quality work that delivers practical solutions for our clients.
A commitment to maintaining high health and safety standards for yourself, your team, and any contractors involved.
Willingness to undertake remote fieldwork across Australia.
Permanent residency in Australia.
An unrestricted Australian driver’s license.

If you’re keen to build your specialist consulting career and contribute to meaningful environmental projects, we’d love you to apply!

You’ll Enjoy These Benefits

Work-Life balance: We help you create space for other important aspects of your life with study breaks and leave purchase plans allowing you to enjoy up to 8 weeks of annual leave per year!
Diverse project opportunities: Work on a wide range of projects across various clients and sectors, keeping your experience fresh and engaging.
Professional growth: Access ongoing development opportunities, including coaching from our approachable technical experts and support for professional memberships.
Employee ownership: Participate in our employee stock purchase plan and share in the company’s success.
Paid parental leave: Enjoy paid parental leave for both primary and secondary caregivers.
Wellbeing support: Access our Employee Assistance Program (EAP), available to all staff and their immediate families.

About Us

Tetra Tech Coffey provides high-end environmental, geotechnical, digital, and engineering design consulting services in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea. Every day, our people come together to solve complex challenges for our clients.

With over 30,000 Tetra Tech colleagues across 550 offices globally, we deliver projects that improve lives through science, technology, and innovation.

Our commitment to creating lasting, measurable value is reflected in our global1 Billion People Challenge, which tracks how our 100,000+ annual projects benefit people and communities around the world.
